summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 69 of CipherBox (FUSE/WinFsp Rust integration + grant-root awareness) — porting the node/v3 model from the TS SDK to the Rust desktop stack, then validate it end-to-end via desktop-e2e per the user's requirement that root-key recovery actually be wired before the phase counts as complete.
summary.outcome: Merged 25 plans covering the full node/v3 port (codec/seal, gated listing, rotation engine, atomic FUSE read/write cutover, JournalOp reshape, grant-scoped delete/rename, recycle-bin/vault-creation migration, legacy-type deletion, and real vault-blob-v3 root-key recovery replacing a placeholder bridge). A live desktop-e2e run against a real API+IPFS+FUSE-T stack passed 4/6 test groups and surfaced a genuine D-07 write-plane pairing bug (now being fixed); only 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows, user's machine) and the D-07 fix + e2e re-run remain.

repo: GSD commit helper reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never retry the commit.

Worktree-isolated executors sometimes mis-report `expected_base` in their metadata (using their own last docs commit instead of the true fork point) — verify via `git merge-base <branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.
`cargo fmt` run on a crate root (e.g. lib.rs) recursively reformats the whole module tree — executors must scope fmt to only their changed files and revert incidental drift before committing.
Fresh worktrees lack `node_modules`, so the husky pre-commit `lint-staged` hook fails on first commit — either run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first or use `--no-verify` for pure-Rust changes.

SC#6 (single gated read entrypoint) and SC#2 (no reencrypt-path leaks) are enforced via CI grep gates in `ci.yml`, with a `// sc6-allow:` marker convention for sanctioned exceptions (recycle-bin, vault-export, replay).

Local desktop-e2e requires macOS binaries built against FUSE-T rather than macFUSE — the `fuser` crate defaults to `mount_macfuse` unless pkg-config finds a `fuse.pc`; CI copies `fuse-t.pc` → `fuse.pc`, sets `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, and applies an rpath fix so the binary loads `libfuse-t.dylib`.
desktop-e2e CI always points `DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL` at `mock-ipns-routing:3001`, never `someguy` (which is prod/staging-only) — local runs must mirror that.
The webview's `/auth/test-login` fetch fails silently ('Load failed') if the API isn't started with `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` including the desktop's origin (`:1420`).
Desktop Tauri build must happen AFTER the frontend `vite build` (or the binary embeds a stale/missing dist) — CI builds frontend, then binary.

code.finding: JournalOp does NOT carry a `parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` field as prior research claimed — that field actually lives in fuse-side `MkdirJournalResult`. Always re-verify grep-derived research claims against the live tree before trusting them for atomicity arguments.

InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File} store ipns_private_key + read/write key material because the FUSE mount is a read-WRITE vault owner (signs IPNS records, seals new children) — unlike the read-only web 68.2 listing client, so ResolvedChild (keyless) cannot directly populate it.

resolve_child unseals the child read-key and immediately zeroizes it (D-09) and never touches the write-body — meaning list_folder/ResolvedChild is read-only and insufficient for a write-owner mount; list_folder_owned (69-17) was added to recover read_key+write_key+ipns_private_key together.
ApiNodeFetcher is a borrow adapter (`{ api: &ApiClient }`) with no `::new` constructor — must be constructed inline at each call site, not stored as a field alongside an owned Arc<ApiClient>.

Prior to 69-24, root read/write keys were derived via a placeholder bridge (`root_write_key = root_read_key ^ 0xA5`) from the legacy single-key vault blob — replaced by real independent random keys recovered from a vault-blob-v3.

vault-blob-v3 format: `0x03 | u16_BE(readLen) | ECIES(rootReadKey) | u16_BE(writeLen) | ECIES(rootWriteKey)` — ported byte-for-byte from packages/core/src/vault/blob.ts and validated against a frozen cross-language KAT (tests/vectors/vault-v3-blob.json).

fetch_splice_publish_parent recovers parent write_children via decode_write_body during replay's parent re-splice — but a live desktop-e2e run surfaced a D-07 pairing bug where a newly-added file child's SealedChildRef (read plane) lands in the parent without a matching WriteChildRef (write plane), causing list_folder_owned to fail with 'no WriteChildRef paired with child node' — root cause not yet isolated at end of transcript.

workflow: When a worktree-isolated executor halts with an architectural blocker (rather than grinding out unverifiable code), verify its grep/blast-radius claims independently before accepting or escalating — agents can be right but should not be trusted uncritically, and can also be overcautious.

For genuinely atomic, unavoidably-large changes (RED mid-flip, no compiling sub-unit), splitting into a committed 'grind runbook' with bounded per-session slices (each landing its own clean commit) lets an atomic flip survive session/usage-limit interruptions without losing coherence.

Gate merges of large crypto/security-sensitive changes on cargo-green PLUS a live end-to-end run, not compile-green alone — this session's D-07 bug shipped clean through unit tests, cross-language KATs, and cargo check, and was only caught by exercising it against a real API+IPFS+FUSE-T stack.

When a plan's dependent infrastructure doesn't exist yet, expanding phase scope with new additive foundation plans (kept independently green) unblocks the dependent plan without destabilizing already-merged work.
Session/usage-limit deaths during agent dispatch are transient and not architectural signals — verify whether any edits landed before re-dispatching identically after the reset.

friction: The gsd-planner and several gsd-executor agents died mid-run from API errors / session usage limits (stalled stream, session cap hit), requiring manual recovery from partial worktree state each time.

Three successive architectural blockers were discovered only during execution (FUSE read/write coupling, missing write-plane emit API, missing write-owner InodeKind materialization) despite prior research and planning passes — research repeatedly underestimated true scope.
The atomic 69-09 FUSE cutover required an 11-slice manual grind across many sessions due to its irreducible size (~12k LOC, no compiling checkpoint until the end).

Local desktop-e2e bring-up hit multiple environment snags: Redis port 6379 already occupied by another project, CORS misconfiguration blocking the webview's test-login fetch, and the binary linking macFUSE instead of the installed FUSE-T.
Bash tool's own 2-minute timeout killed a long-running e2e suite invocation before its inner `timeout 700` could complete, requiring a background re-run.
One scratchpad handoff was initially written to a doubled/incorrect path and had to be moved.
open_items: D-07 write-plane pairing bug (missing WriteChildRef when a parent republishes after a new file child) is being root-caused/fixed by a dispatched debugger agent; desktop-e2e must be re-run to confirm all 6 test groups pass once fixed.
69-14 (WinFsp/Windows, autonomous:false) remains — requires the user's Windows machine; platform/windows/* edits were made best-effort during the grind but are unverified locally.
ROT-07: shared-scope-exit deletes/moves on Unix fail closed (EIO) because no production RotationDeps implementor is wired yet — secure-by-default but functionally incomplete.
Merge of origin/main into the phase branch was in progress (STATE.md conflict resolved) with the merge commit not yet confirmed/verified green at transcript end.
Known accepted E2E risks documented but unverified: file `versions` not reconstructed on write, file_iv hex round-trip correctness, orphaned parent-CID pins not unpinned after republish.
Phase branch not yet pushed / no PR opened as of end of transcript.
